claims.text: Aging an AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy at approximately 650°C for 2 hours will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates along eutectic interfaces.
The proposed aging treatment will increase yield strength relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed aging treatment will increase ductility relative to the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
An inert argon atmosphere prevents oxidation during the aging treatment.
The aging intervention is applicable to bulk samples.
Optimizing aging time and temperature can avoid precipitate coarsening.
The aging treatment forms uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates at eutectic-lamella interfaces.
The nanoscale precipitates refine phase boundaries.
The nanoscale interfacial precipitates improve load transfer between the eutectic phases.
The introduced nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
The introduced nanoscale precipitates homogenize strain distribution.
Mitigating stress concentration at phase boundaries can enhance ductility in eutectic alloys.
The beneficial strength-and-ductility response depends on retaining precipitates at nanoscale dimensions.
Coarser precipitates may nullify the improvements or reduce ductility through embrittlement.
The proposed approach has been specifically validated for the AlCoCrFeNi-based alloy system under inert atmospheric conditions.
The treatment can be tested by aging samples for 1–3 hours at 630–670°C and comparing them with untreated as-cast samples.
TEM, hardness mapping, tensile testing, and fractography will be used to characterize precipitates, mechanical properties, and interface integrity.
Failure to improve both yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast baseline falsifies the hypothesis.
